points.t: ‘Urticaria’ where **each wheal lasts > 24 h**, burns or hurts, and leaves **bruising or brown staining**.
**Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis**; low C3 / C4 and anti-C1q in the hypocomplementaemic form.
Mark a wheal to time it; complement, ESR / CRP, urine, ANA; **refer for biopsy**; antihistamines help itch, not the vasculitis.
**HUVS** with lupus, kidney, lung (COPD-like) or eye involvement.

points: **Hypocomplementaemic** (~20–30%): systemic; severe form **HUVS** (anti-C1q vasculitis) with arthritis, angioedema, eye inflammation, COPD, glomerulonephritis; overlaps **SLE**.
Causes: **drugs** (ACE-i, penicillins, sulfonamides, NSAIDs, TNF inhibitors…), **CTD**, **paraproteins** (IgM: Schnitzler), cryoglobulins, malignancy, hepatitis B / C, EBV, Lyme; idiopathic.

features.lead: Time it, feel it, look at what it leaves.
points: Each lesion **> 24 h (often 1–3 days)** vs < 24 h in ordinary urticaria.
Resolves leaving **purpura / bruising or brown pigment**.
Systemic: fever, arthralgia, abdominal pain, angioedema, nodes; eye / kidney / lung in HUVS.

visuals.caption: Circle a wheal with a pen and photograph it daily. An ordinary wheal is gone within 24 hours; urticarial vasculitis persists for days and leaves a bruise-like stain.
visuals.alt: Three days of a pen-circled wheal ending as a bruise

points: H&E + **DIF** of a lesion < 48 h old: LCV.
**C3, C4, C1q, anti-C1q**, CH50; ANA, dsDNA, ENA; ESR / CRP, FBC, U&E, LFT; hepatitis B / C, HIV; SPEP, cryoglobulins.

cards.name: Chronic spontaneous urticaria
cards.clue: Wheals < 24 h, itch, normal skin after, antihistamine-responsive.

cards.name: SLE
cards.clue: Photosensitivity, ANA +, low complement, nephritis; ~50% of HUVS meet SLE criteria.

manage.lead: Refer; find the cause; specialist ladder.

points: **Refer** dermatology ± rheumatology / renal (urgent if renal involvement).
Non-sedating antihistamines (itch / angioedema, not vasculitis); NSAIDs only if renal function allows.

**Dapsone, colchicine, hydroxychloroquine** (mild / normocomplementaemic) → oral steroids for flares → **mycophenolate, azathioprine, methotrexate** → **rituximab** (HUVS / SLE); omalizumab (case reports); anakinra / canakinumab (Schnitzler); cyclophosphamide / MMF for nephritis.
Dapsone: FBC, LFT, methaemoglobin. HCQ: annual eye screening after 5 years (from 1 year if risk factors, RCOphth 2020). MMF: FBC / LFT; contraception.

items.t: Wheals with **joint pain, fever, abdominal pain, breathlessness or abnormal urine**: suspected systemic (hypocomplementaemic) disease.
Wheals > 24 h, burning or bruising: dermatology for biopsy.

pearls.t: **Wheals that last more than a day, burn, and leave a bruise = biopsy.**
Pen-circle and photograph a wheal daily: cheap, effective timing.
Low C3 / C4 / C1q → hunt for lupus, kidney and lung disease.

quiz.a: Complement: low C3, C4, C1q; anti-C1q.
